business_scope.primary_industry_name: Delivery-Only Multi-Brand Cloud Kitchen Facility Operations

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (EU-harmonized; French-inspired commercial law with autonomous partnership legislation for the SCSp)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU Common Commercial Policy: EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (in force) and EU-Canada CETA (provisionally applicable) apply to Luxembourg
Luxembourg-United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1996, as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
Luxembourg-Switzerland Double Taxation Convention (1993, as amended)
Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment protection agreements concluded before the EU assumed exclusive competence, where still active

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, as amended (including Laws of 10 August 2018 and 25 March 2020); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and its grand-ducal implementing regulation; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCSL), as amended; Law of 23 July 2016 on Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, and applicable CSSF circulars on customer due diligence, PEPs and sanctions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite spéciale), executed as a private deed or, where real property is contributed or notarial form is elected, as a Luxembourg notarial deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary for notarial deeds; otherwise RCSL-filed private deed with authenticated signatures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign executed signatures; otherwise consular legalization at the competent Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports, proof of residential address and source-of-funds documentation for each natural-person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority in the UBO's country of origin (police, registry, municipality or financial institution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or official company excerpt for any foreign corporate general partner or corporate limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent official body of the entity's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the 1961 Hague Convention; if not a party, bilateral consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD before formation: identify and verify all UBOs at or above the 25% ownership threshold; screen all general partners, limited partners, UBOs and signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN, CSSF/Luxembourg FIU lists, and Interpol notices; enhanced due diligence for PEPs, politically exposed persons and high-risk third countries; source of wealth and source of funds must be evidenced; files retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés / Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL/LBR) online portal — www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: RCSL filings are accepted in French; statutes may be in French, German or Luxembourgish. Foreign-language documents submitted for pre-incorporation clearance must be accompanied by a sworn French translation. The registered name must be in Latin characters; non-Latin brand scripts must be transliterated or transcribed into Latin script. The legal-form suffix 'SCSp' or 'société en commandite spéciale' must appear immediately after the commercial name and may not be omitted.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANQUE / BANK / BANKING — prior CSSF authorization required
ASSURANCE / RÉASSURANCE / INSURANCE — prior Commissariat aux Assurances authorization required
SICAV / SICAF / OPC / OPCVM / UCITS / FONDS / FUND — regulated investment fund or product regime required
LUXEMBOURG / ÉTAT / STATE / GOVERNMENT / COMMUNE / MUNICIPAL — false public authority implication prohibited
CHAMBRE DE COMMERCE / CHAMBRE DES MÉTIERS — statutorily protected chamber names
UE / EU / BCE / ECB / EURO — false official European Union or monetary affiliation prohibited
SARL / S.A. / SCA / SCS — legal form suffixes that misrepresent the entity as a corporate entity are prohibited for an SCSp
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCSL name check is rejected, the applicant may immediately submit a revised name or file a written administrative review request with the RCSL registrar, including evidence of prior usage, trademark rights, and explanation of non-confusion. A further adverse decision may be challenged before the Luxembourg administrative tribunal (recours en annulation) within three months from notification; interim suspension (référé) may be sought for urgent harm. No formal extension of the 30-day name acceptance window is available; a fresh availability check is required after expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the statutory seat of an SCSp. A physical registered office in Luxembourg, at which legal process and correspondence can be served, is mandatory. A virtual office or PO box may only supplement, not replace, the physical seat. For a ghost kitchen operator, a commercial lease and food-business operating licence at the delivery-only kitchen location are separate substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 20%-30% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months after RCSL registration; the probability increases to more than 50% after the first corporate tax/VAT filing if invoices show related-party platform payments, thin local headcount, or a pattern inconsistent with physical supply, in which case the Luxembourg registration of virtual brands will be inspected by tax and food-safety authorities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCSL tariff; online search is free; blocking certificate priced at statutory fixed fee.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/UBO pre-incorporation dossier: CDD documents, apostilles, source-of-funds collation, sanctions/PEP screening and foreign corporate verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg corporate law firm and, where engaged, a registered CAS/PSF agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fee of EUR 350-500, excluding VAT.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and certification of the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite spéciale)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm; Luxembourg notary if real property is contributed or notarial form is elected
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: EUR 1,800-2,500 fixed fee, excluding VAT and notarial disbursements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of UBO passports, foreign company good-standing certificates and proof of source of funds
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in country of issue; Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate where consular legalization is required

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation of all non-French/German/Luxembourgish documents into French

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court-appointed translator tariff; approximate per-word rate with minimum per document.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL registration and RESA statutory publication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCSL filing fee and RESA publication fee under the statutory fee schedule.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE beneficial-owner filing and registered-office verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE service) / Ministry of Justice

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Title III, Articles 322-1 to 322-12, as introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016 on the SCSp), together with the Law of 28 January 2019 on the modernisation of Luxembourg company law.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the authority of the Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association / Limited Partnership Agreement (contrat de société) of the SCSp, executed by notarial deed or by private written instrument and filed electronically with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - the SCSp has no legal minimum capital requirement; capital is freely fixed by the partnership agreement and may be contributed in cash, in kind or as services. No statutory escrow or blocked account is required, although a bank certificate evidencing the limited partners' initial contribution is recommended for RCS and financing purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founding general partner(s) approve the incorporation of [●] SCSp under the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the subscription of partnership interests by the limited partners, as recorded in the contribution schedule, is approved and adopted in full. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [●], Luxembourg, and the general partner(s) are authorized to execute the notarial deed and file it with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [●] is appointed managing general partner (gérant), acting alone, with full power to register the partnership for VAT and social security, obtain the establishment authorization, open bank accounts, and execute all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement (contrat de société)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (or, where no real estate is contributed, a private deed between the partners); registered office address confirmed by the local commune.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement containing the corporate name, registered office, corporate object (operation of a delivery-only multi-brand cloud kitchen), term, classes of partnership interests, contribution regime and the powers of the general partner (gérant). Obtain the landlord's written consent to the registered office. Execute the deed before a notary when real property or a real right is contributed or when the financing transaction requires a notarial act; otherwise execute by private signed writing. The instrument must state the identity, address and profession of the general partner(s) and of each limited partner, together with the amount and form of contributions.
required_dossiers: Valid national identity card or passport of each general and limited partner
Certified proof of residential address of each partner (utility bill, bailment or notarial certificate)
Draft limited partnership agreement / articles of association
Bank certificate evidencing the initial contribution (if any)
Written consent of the landlord for the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the registry queries incomplete or defective clauses, execute an addendum rectificatif to the partnership agreement and resubmit the consolidated text before the scheduled RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the incorporation deed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS - Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Luxembourg Business Registers online filing portal www.lbr.lu).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed incorporation deed and the statutory annexures through the RCS online filing channel or at the RCS counter. Pay the statutory registration fee. Upon verification by the RCS registrar, obtain the RCS registration number (numéro d'immatriculation) and the official corporate identity excerpt. Legal effects vis-à-vis third parties attach as of the RCS filing, although the SCSp technically exists as of the signature of the deed.
required_dossiers: Executed notarial or private deed of the SCSp partnership agreement
Statutory declaration on honour by the general partner(s) concerning absence of criminal conviction (déclaration de non-condamnation)
Proof of registered office address (lease, ownership title or landlord's consent)
Identification documents of the general partner(s)
Payment receipt of the RCS filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS registrar issues an observation, cure the deficiency within the granted delay (generally 8 days) by filing the corrected document in the required language via the e-filing channel; otherwise resubmit the application with a new filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA Electronic Compendium
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS validation, the registration particulars are transmitted to RESA for official publication. Verify the published notice containing the corporate name, the form (SCSp), the registered office, the RCS identifier and the corporate object. Publication must occur within one month of the RCS filing to render the incorporation opposable to third parties and to complete the statutory publicity requirement.
required_dossiers: RCS filing confirmation receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA notice contains errors, request a corrigendum through LBR customer services; if publication is not effected within one month, file a written request for expedited publication to the RCS registrar and, if necessary, refile the corrected data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT (TVA) registration with the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); application via the AEDT forms or the Guichet.lu portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Luxembourg VAT registration form (Formulaire 563) and identify the taxable activity: delivery-only prepared food supply carried out by the ghost kitchen. Indicate the applicable VAT treatment of restaurant and delivery supplies, the accounting period and bank references. Upon approval, obtain the Luxembourg VAT number (no. TVA LU...) and the VAT identification certificate. Registration is mandatory for every taxable person carrying out economic activity in Luxembourg, regardless of revenue level.
required_dossiers: RCS excerpt (extrait du RCS) evidencing the SCSp registration
VAT registration form (Form 563)
Identity documents of the general partner(s)
Description of the cloud kitchen / food service activities
Projected turnover and business plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT requests additional information, respond in writing via the assigned case officer or through MyGuichet; if the application is not processed within the statutory delay, file a formal reminder and, where applicable, request waiver of late-interest where the delay is attributable to the administration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment authorization (Autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) - Directorate-General for Industry; applications channelled through the Guichet.lu one-stop shop and the Ministry's establishment authorization department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply on Guichet.lu under the sector 'HORECA / Restauration' for the authorization to operate 'Restaurants and mobile food service activities' (NACE 56.10). Demonstrate the good repute of the general partner(s) and, where applicable, the professional competence of the operational manager in food service management. The authorization is personal to the operator and must be obtained before the commencement of the economic activity; the owner/operator model under an SCSp requires the authorized person to be the actual operating manager or a designated qualified manager.
required_dossiers: Completed establishment authorization application form
Certificate of good conduct (bulletin n°3) of the general partner(s) and operational manager
Proof of professional qualification (diploma, certification or at least 3 years' practical experience in food service management)
RCS excerpt confirming the SCSp registration
Identity card or passport of the applicant(s)
Description of the kitchen premises and operational plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authorization is refused, the applicant may file a hierarchical administrative appeal with the Minister of the Economy within three months of the notification, or submit a derogation request supported by evidence of equivalent professional experience or qualifications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food business registration, municipal clearance and fire-technical inspection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration luxembourgeoise vétérinaire et alimentaire (ALVA) under the Ministry of Health; municipal authority (bourgmestre) of the commune of the kitchen; communal fire prevention commission with the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the cloud kitchen as a food business operator (FBO) with ALVA under Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 and Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 before commencement; submit the HACCP-based plan, the kitchen layout and the waste management arrangements. Obtain the municipal commodo/incommodo assessment or notice of no-objection, the fire safety clearance (inspection of kitchen extraction hood, extinguishers and escape routes), and the occupational health and safety statement where employees will be engaged.
required_dossiers: Food business operator registration form with ALVA
HACCP documentation and food safety procedures
Kitchen floor plan with waste, ventilation and refrigeration layout
Municipal commodo/incommodo or building permit and structural load certificate
Fire safety inspection report (extraction hood suppression, extinguishers, evacuation routes, alarms)
Waste management and used cooking oil disposal contract (tracking notes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ALVA or the commune raises deficiencies, correct the structural, hygiene or fire-safety items and reschedule an inspection; fire clearance non-compliance is cured by remediation works followed by a reinspection by the CGDIS or communal fire officers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) - Directorate-General for Industry, in conjunction with the Administration luxembourgeoise vétérinaire et alimentaire (ALVA) for food hygiene approval.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Authorization) for NACE 56.10, together with the ALVA Food Business Operator Registration Certificate under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Department of the Environment), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity; wastewater aspects handled with the Administration de la gestion de l'eau.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA for standard multi-brand cloud kitchen facilities below the thresholds of Annexes I and II of the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; a simplified environmental notice or Class 4 commodo/incommodo registration under the Law of 10 June 1999 on Classified Establishments (as amended) may apply where installed kitchen capacity, odour output or refrigeration loads are significant.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 24 November 1989 and municipal sewer ordinances - pH 6-10, COD ≤ 1000 mg/l, TSS ≤ 600 mg/l, fats/oils ≤ 100 mg/l, with grease traps and sampling points installed. VOCs and odours: compliance with Directive 2010/75/EU and national thresholds, with activated carbon or equivalent odour abatement on extraction stacks if complaints or capacity exceed prescribed limits. Solid waste: segregated food waste, cardboard and used cooking oil collection with waste transfer notes under the Law of 21 March 2012 on Waste Management and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 9 December 2021.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) through the communal fire commission, verifying manual and automatic extinguishers, commercial kitchen extraction-hood suppression, emergency exits, alarming and evacuation routes; structural load inspection certificate for kitchen equipment, hoods and refrigeration installations issued by a certified civil matter expert; occupational health and safety clearance delivered by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering ventilation, electrical conformity, sanitary facilities, thermal stress and manual-handling risk assessments under Articles L-210-1 et seq. of the Luxembourg Labour Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in conjunction with the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as banking and payment-entity supervisor. No separate foreign-exchange control administration exists; Luxembourg adheres to EU TFEU Articles 63-65 on free movement of capital and the euro-zone single currency regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions. The euro is the lawful currency and is freely transferable without exchange-control approval. For the SCSp structure, profit remittances to resident and non-resident partners are unrestricted; the only conditioning factors are (i) CSSF/BCL statistical balance-of-payments reporting for each cross-border flow of EUR 12,500 or more and (ii) compliance with anti-money-laundering rules and the Luxembourg law of 12 July 2013 on the Special Limited Partnership. No capital-account license or prior authorisation is required for foreign direct investment into a Luxembourg SCSp, nor for distributions of profits, repayment of partner loans, or liquidation proceeds. The ghost kitchen's delivery aggregator receivables are current-account services income, payable in EUR, USD, or any freely convertible currency at the parties' election.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no surrender, mandatory conversion, deposit, or repatriation timeline for export or services receipts. Invoices settled in EUR or foreign currency may be retained offshore at the commercial discretion of the SCSp. The sole obligation is indirect: banks report cross-border payment statistics to the BCL, and the SCSp must be able to evidence the commercial substance of aggregator settlements on demand.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account (EUR/USD) with SEPA and SWIFT connectivity
Operational account with e-banking payment factory and merchant payout aggregation
Capital escrow account and operational treasury account
Operational account for trade disbursements and FX hedging collateral

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: KBL European Private Bankers (Quintet Private Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Private-banking-focused operational account for high-net-worth partner assets

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility. CSSF-authorised electronic money institutions and payment institutions (e.g., licensed EMI platforms operating under the Luxembourg law of 10 November 2009 on payment services) may provide IBAN accounts, virtual account management, and aggregator payout collection. However, a pure fintech EMI cannot serve as the SCSp's primary treasury bank because the SCSp has no minimum capital and no legal personality, which triggers enhanced due diligence; EMIs are legally prohibited from accepting deposits and from executing credit operations. Their viable role is limited to the collection layer for UberEats and DoorDash settlement sweeps and to automated currency conversion at specified anchor rates, while Tier-1 correspondent clearing rails must settle final liquidity. Cross-border EMIs on passported EU licences are usable for low-value daily receivable sweeps, but the master treasury account must remain at an authorised credit institution under CSSF consolidated supervision.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is required for at least one general partner (gérant) or its legal representative and, in practice, for the ultimate beneficial owners of the SCSp at the initial onboarding meeting. Tier-1 Luxembourg banks demand an in-person interview at their premises or with a registered local agent holding a power of attorney. Remote onboarding is generally not permitted for SCSp structures with non-resident limited partners; a notarised power of attorney and apostilled documentary pack may allow a local accountant to represent the SCSp at the interview, but the responsible person must appear. Digital-only onboarding without any physical step is available exclusively at fintech EMIs, and those accounts are functionally restricted to low-value operational flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp has no statutory minimum capital and a partnership register showing multiple non-resident limited partners; bank flags 'absence of substantive commercial asset basis'.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a notarised partnership agreement, the register of partners, the registered office lease with at least 12-month term, the RCS extract issued within 30 days, the RSSS (social security) registration, a management resolution designating the account signatories, and a source-of-funds file for each LP (tax returns, dividend vouchers, sale deeds, or bank statements of the originating account).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receivables derive exclusively from high-frequency, low-ticket food delivery aggregator payouts (UberEats and DoorDash), which the bank may classify as 'aggregator-dependent and chargeback-sensitive'.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide signed master service agreements with UberEats and DoorDash, the payout schedule showing settlement T+1 to T+5 cycles, the kitchen facility lease evidencing real operational premises, three months of projected order volumes, historical chargeback and refund statistics, and a legal memorandum confirming that the SCSp is not performing regulated payment services but is merely a merchant receiving payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SCSp operates multiple virtual brands under trademarks held by affiliated or third-party entities; bank suspects unlicensed brand use or hidden royalty leakage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle the trademark licence agreements, register of trademarks from the Luxembourg IP Office (RGDP) or EUIPO, arm's-length royalty benchmarking consistent with OECD transfer pricing guidelines, and a transfer pricing documentation file proving that brand royalties correspond to identifiable services and are subject to Luxembourg tax-transparent reporting at the partner level.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No employees in Luxembourg and kitchen labour outsourced to staffing agencies; bank questions the SCSp's 'commercial substance' and management control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present the staff-leasing contract with a licensed temporary-work agency, payroll and social security declarations of hired personnel, food-hygiene operating licenses, and a corporate substance memorandum describing the SCSp's control over procurement, brand strategy, data analytics, and menu engineering. The SCSp must document that the delivery platform integrations are contractually operated from Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Operational kitchens are located in other jurisdictions while the SCSp is registered in Luxembourg; bank identifies a permanent establishment or cross-border payroll exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the intercompany service arrangement between the Luxembourg SCSp and the foreign operating kitchen entity, a permanent establishment analysis confirming where taxable substance sits, payroll registration certificates of the jurisdiction where kitchen staff are employed, and tax counsel's opinion that income flows have economic substance and are priced on an arm's-length basis.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from partners must be routed through correspondent banking channels using SWIFT MT103 or TARGET2 transfers. In the SWIFT field 70 (Remittance Information), the payment must state 'CONSTITUTION OF CAPITAL - SCSP [Registered Office Reference]' and the beneficiary account must be the SCSp's dedicated capital escrow account opened under the partnership's name. For BCL balance-of-payments reporting, contributions above EUR 12,500 are coded as direct investment equity capital (BOP category: FDI inflow, equity, euro), and the bank will require the remitter's name to match the partner register of the SCSp. The escrow account releases funds to the operating account only upon presentation of the notarised contribution statement. For non-EU inbound wires in USD, the receiving Luxembourg bank converts through its own FX engine, applying the ECB reference rate plus a defined spread; the SCSp must instruct the bank to settle the conversion as 'spot delivery' and to allocate the proceeds on the same value date to the operational treasury ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails comprise: (i) SEPA Credit Transfers for all EUR-denominated intra-EU payments to suppliers, landlords, and staff-leasing agencies; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border payments for raw materials, imported kitchen equipment, and brand royalties outside the euro-zone; (iii) commercial letters of credit governed by UCP600 for high-value equipment purchases from non-EU overseas suppliers; (iv) SEPA B2B Direct Debit for recurring utilities; and (v) the aggregator payout rails of UberEats and DoorDash, which sweep merchant settlements directly into the SCSp's segregated collection account. Disbursement policy requires that outbound payments be initiated only after final aggregator settlement and the expiry of the chargeback-protection window; intra-day liquidity is managed through a notional liquidity pool at the Luxembourg lead bank to ensure that MT103 payments are never released on an unsecured intra-day overdraft basis.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable EUR/USD forwards with tenors of 1 to 12 months, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a CSSF-authorised credit institution; used to hedge committed aggregator settlement revenues denominated in USD.
Outright deliverable EUR/GBP forwards, with the same tenors and documentation, for UK-DoorDash and Deliveroo-style payout exposure.
FX swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/GBP) used exclusively for treasury liquidity management and matching of the SCSp's two-currency receivable and payable cycles.
European-style EUR/USD currency options for contingent currency exposure arising from franchise acquisitions and equipment purchases, where a forward would create a firm commitment risk.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for exotic currency exposures (EUR/THB, EUR/PHP, EUR/AED) where a deliverable forward market is unavailable in the SCSp's operating jurisdictions; such instruments must be cash-settled and documented under a cross-currency master agreement.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps solely to hedge matched lease or debt-financing obligations of the SCSp, provided the notional amount does not exceed the underlying committed liability and the counterparty meets a minimum credit rating of A-.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS declaration (déclaration annuelle de maintien au registre)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) month after each anniversary of the initial RCS registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers administrative late-fee assessments of EUR 10 per month; continuous failure for two consecutive years exposes the SCSp to RCS administrative strike-off and judicial winding-up procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (déclaration annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs – UBO register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – UBO Register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs / RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) month after the RCS registration anniversary each year; simultaneous with the annual RCS declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission carries criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment; additionally, voting and distribution rights may be suspended until the register is compliant.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) deposit – mandatory only if the SCSp meets statutory filing thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven (7) months after the end of the financial year (available extension to eight (8) months under conditions)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties range from EUR 100 to EUR 10,000 plus a EUR 10 per day penalty; continued default after formal notice may lead to RCS strike-off and judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Collective income tax declaration (déclaration collective des revenus) for tax transparent SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg direct tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June following the close of the taxable year (where year-end = 31 December); extended deadlines granted on group filing schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing interest accrues at 0.6% per month on any assessed tax; administrative penalty up to EUR 250,000 for repeated non-compliance; default assessments may be issued ex officio.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For an SCSp, statutory mandatory audit applies where at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: (i) balance-sheet total exceeding EUR 4,400,000; (ii) net turnover exceeding EUR 8,800,000; (iii) average workforce exceeding 50 employees. An audit is also mandatory if the partnership agreement expressly requires or if consolidated annual accounts of the LBR/legal group require it. Micro and small SCSp entities satisfying the scope exemptions are exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2019 transposing Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for the statutory annual accounts where the SCSp is part of a consolidated group.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must file a beneficial ownership declaration with the Luxembourg Business Registers within 30 days of any transfer that changes qualifying beneficial ownership; an annual confirmation must be filed each calendar year within one month of the RCS anniversary. The annual confirmation certifies the completeness of the RBE register and covers all direct/indirect ownership details obtained under the 13 January 2019 UBO law. Interim share transfers may be recorded by notarial or private deed; the register is the operative source.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Register of Limited Partners)
Minute Book (resolutions and written deliberations of associates)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 324 – USD 1,620 per annum (typical Luxembourg registered office / corporate agent service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,240 – USD 8,640 per annum (typical certified audit fee for a small/medium SCSp)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate Luxembourg CIT rate for the 2025 financial year, composed of 17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge on the CIT, and 6.75% municipal business tax applicable in Luxembourg City; the exact municipal component varies by commune.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory corporate income tax holiday is available to ghost kitchen operators. An SCSp is tax transparent and generally exempt from entity-level CIT; profits flow to partners who are taxed under their own residence regimes. Qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary exemption and the Luxembourg participation exemption may reduce the effective rate to 0% on qualifying share income. The investment tax credit for digital assets and energy-efficient kitchen equipment can lower the effective rate by approximately 8% to 12% of qualifying expenditure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 520 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and Form 521 (municipal business tax declaration) filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu, with supporting schedules submitted to the Administration des contributions directes (Tax Office VI for Luxembourg companies).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax return must be filed on or before the last day of the sixth month following the fiscal year-end, unless an extension is granted in writing by the Luxembourg tax administration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SCSp registered office, Luxembourg trade registry number, date of incorporation and fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident general partners must append their foreign corporate ID, tax residence certificate and, where applicable, VAT number; a local tax representative may complete and file the return on their behalf.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book profit or loss per the annual financial statements, adjusted for tax-exempt income, non-deductible expenses, and fiscal corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SCSp is fiscally transparent, the entity itself leaves the tax basis lines blank; partners declare the allocated share of profit or loss in their own returns. A taxable corporate partner or an opaque SCSp files the full amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed statement of management fees, franchise royalties, platform service fees, delivery technology charges and interest paid to related parties, including UberEats and DoorDash aggregator entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owner must attach contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation proving arm's length rates; deductibility is denied if the documentation is absent or insufficient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward and set off against current taxable income, respecting the statutory carryforward cap of five years for this pipeline assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a transparent SCSp are allocated directly to partners; Luxembourg-resident corporate partners apply Luxembourg loss rules, while non-resident partners apply their own home country loss mechanisms.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties range from EUR 250 to EUR 10,000 per return; a daily surcharge of up to EUR 50 can be applied until the return is submitted; late payment interest accrues at 0.9% per month or fraction thereof; gross negligence surcharge can reach 50% of the understated tax, increasing to 100% in cases of deliberate evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg withholding tax applies to dividends paid by a Luxembourg resident corporate entity; a transparent SCSp is not an opaque corporation, so partnership distributions to partners are generally treated as capital allocations and are exempt from dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A partner seeking DTA relief must deliver to the Luxembourg paying agent: (i) a Form 558 certificate of Luxembourg tax residence or a certified statement of partnership allocation, (ii) a current Tax Residence Certificate issued by the partner's home tax authority, and (iii) a beneficial ownership declaration. Complete documentation must be submitted before payment is executed; otherwise withholding is applied at the statutory rate and the excess may be reclaimed through a Luxembourg refund claim within five years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law does not impose any withholding tax on arm's-length royalties or interest paid to non-residents (0%). Treaty rates are therefore immaterial unless Luxembourg anti-abuse rules reclassify the payment as a constructive dividend, in which case the 15% domestic dividend withholding tax may apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: For taxpayers within the administrative scope of the Luxembourg TP guidelines, a contemporaneous Local File is mandatory when annual related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000, while a Master File is statistically expected for groups with consolidated revenues above EUR 750,000,000 under the Country-by-Country Reporting framework; for a medium-sized SCSp ghost kitchen network, intercompany platform fees, brand royalties and delivery commissions above EUR 100,000 must be supported by an internal pricing documentation memorandum.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg is not an Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) jurisdiction in the Gulf/UAE sense, but the same substance doctrine is enforced through the EU ATAD GAAR, Luxembourg domestic GAAR and treaty abuse case law. A ghost kitchen SCSp must demonstrate local decision-making, employee presence, operational premises, delivery management capacity, and genuine commercial activity in Luxembourg; otherwise profits are reattributed to the ultimate beneficial owners and claims under tax treaties may be denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion - false returns and hidden delivery income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of cash-delivery sales, omission of UberEats/DoorDash settlement reports, creation of artificial franchise invoices, or destruction of sales ledger records from virtual brand channels.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud fines up to EUR 250,000 and recovery of the entire evaded CIT, plus a fraud penalty of up to 100% of the evaded tax; late payment penalties continue to accrue on the outstanding amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing partners and directors are jointly and severally liable for the tax delinquency if they signed or directed the false declarations; imprisonment from 2 to 10 years, civil restitution of the evaded amounts, travel bans pending payment, and prohibition from managing Luxembourg companies for a fixed period.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company abuse and artificial structuring
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp incorporated solely as a pass-through conduit to shift ghost kitchen profits to non-resident zero-tax partners without local staff, premises, commercial risks, or delivery operations, while maintaining the Luxembourg letterbox in an unrelated serviced office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax administration will disregard the SCSp under the GAAR, reassess the true operator as the taxable owner, impose CIT at up to 24.94%, deny deductions for all intercompany platform and royalty fees, and apply a gross negligence penalty of 50%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner becomes personally liable for the reassessed corporate taxes if assets were stripped from the SCSp; civil restitution orders are issued for the profit shifted, travel restrictions may be imposed until the treasury claim is secured, and criminal sanctions include 1 to 5 years imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and KYC failure on online delivery payouts
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting UberEats and DoorDash payouts through unverified bank accounts, withholding beneficial ownership information, or routing settlement funds through offshore nominees without performing client due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties under Luxembourg AML legislation of up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual worldwide turnover; suspension or revocation of the mandatory food business health license and commercial registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held civilly liable for laundering the proceeds of unlicensed food operations, subject to confiscation of the delivery revenues, a five-year ban on serving as a director, and imprisonment from 2 to 5 years for intentional AML breaches.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing non-compliance and documentation failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying supra-normal brand royalties or delivery platform fees to related entities without an arm's length study, booking a guaranteed profit margin to the Luxembourg operator, and failing to maintain updated Local File records for six accounting years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax office disallows the uncontrolled intercompany deductions, computes an upward adjustment to taxable income, imposes penalties of up to EUR 10,000 for non-production of scheduled TP documentation and daily fines for continued non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: In an insolvent SCSp, the taxable general partner is personally assessed for the underpaid tax; directors who signed audit reports knowing the transfer pricing positions lack substance may face criminal fines, restitution to the state, and a maximum five-year prison sentence.
